## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suttādhiṭṭhānatatiyabhūmi* ("The Third Stage: The Terminology of the Discourses") is the third section of the *Peṭakopadesa*, an interpretive and methodological treatise preserved within the Pali Khuddaka collection [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral]. The secondary literature excerpts matched in the dossier do not discuss this work, consisting entirely of spurious hits for the biblical Epistles of Peter or Tibetan mantra syllables.
SuttaCentral identifies curated passage-level parallels between this text and the preceding chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi*), as well as the corresponding *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* section of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral]. It also notes that specific verses and discourses are cited or discussed within the chapter, including *Dhammapada* verses (Dhp 231, 233, 246, 281, 349) and their parallels across the Patna Dharmapada, Tibetan, and Chinese collections (T 210, T 212, T 213, Udānavarga), the *Verasutta* (AN 5.174), and the Sanskrit *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analyses from DharmaNexus confirm the heavy intertextuality of the work, reporting 994 Pali-internal matches across 72 canonical and post-canonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, notably the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4, with §56.1–58.4 matching AN 4.52), *Ekakanipāta* (AN 1), *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5, where §10.1–12.1 matches AN 5.174), *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), and *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares significant textual material with the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 12, SN 16, and SN 48), the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 129), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the *Nettippakaraṇa* (where §34.7–35.3 corresponds closely to Ne 37 §391.5–392.4, agreeing with SuttaCentral's parallel), and later subcommentarial literature such as the *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Sanskrit collections (the Udānavarga, Patna Dharmapada, and *Arthaviniścayasūtra*), Chinese translations including the *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125) and *Dīrghāgama* (T 1), and Tibetan translations of canonical sūtras and scholastic treatises [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
